newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK to remain free, non-interventionist - Tsang.
newsitem.headline: HK to remain free, non-interventionist - Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary Donald Tsang on Tuesday rejected calls for government intervention in the economy, charging it as counter-productive and putting pressure on resources in the long-run.

While proponents of an interventionist policy had always argued it would prevent unemployment, maintain a more balanced economy and provide a vision for future development, Tsang said intervention would not yield such lofty results.
"These are worthy goals, but government intervention to reverse market forces will not produce such results," Tsang said at a business conference.
Neither was going against free and fair competition as the way for Hong Kong to respond to challenges, Tsang said.
"In Hong Kong, we create new jobs and boost production by providing entrepreneurs and investors with the right environment," he said.
Freewheeling Hong Kong, unlike most Asian economies, has always given free rein to private enterprise.

But slower growth in recent years have prompted calls for an interventionist policy, to rescue declining industries and strike a balance between the manufacturing and service sectors. But Tsang was not convinced.
"The more that politicians and bureaucrats abandon economic planning and economic controls, the more room they create for enterprise, productivity and economic growth," he added.
Tsang also pointed out that any deviation from the current policy of non-intervention would amount to a retreat from the capitalist system and an advance towards socialist policies.
